the pigeons' responding to the middle-sized probe stimulus was determined by its similarity to the S+ of the prevailing discrimination, and not by the similarity of the probe set as a whole to the prevailing discrimination.

the nature and development of the control of stimulus-response relationships by stimulus characteristics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the behavior of the pigeon in the present situation was determined solely by the absolute size differences among the stimuli, and that the behavior was not determined by the relative position of the stimuli in the discrimination set, by the relative position in the discrimination sequence, or by the relative position within a probe.
, in the present experiment, the birds' responses were determined primarily by the similarity of the probe stimulus to the prevailing discrimination stimulus.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the birds responded to the stimulus that was closest in size to either the positive or negative member of the prevailing discrimination, or to the stimulus that had been reinforced most recently.
the pigeons responded to stimuli on the basis of their absolute sizes, and not to their relations to each other or to the prevailing discrimination S+.
pigeons learn to respond to stimuli that have been correlated with reward.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the birds learned to respond to stimuli on the basis of absolute size.
pigeons are able to learn and retain a discrimination between the sizes of stimuli.
